newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AUSTRALIA SEMIS - Get first supply in weeks.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AUSTRALIA SEMIS - Get first supply in weeks.

text.p: TCV NSW T-CORP QTC
*The semis market saw its first supply in over a month with Queensland Treasury Corp (QTC) tendering A$100 million of stock.
*No reaction to Western Australia election call last week.
The Australian semi-government bond market saw its first supply in over a month with Queensland Treasury Corp (QTC) tendering A$100 million of stock.

The tender of QTC's June 2005 bonds went off at a weighted average yield of 7.272 percent with accepted bids in a tight 7.265-7.280 bid range, and 17.2 basis over the Australian Treasury's 2005 stock. The outstanding stock was seen quoted at around 7.30/7.26 percent when tender bids went in this morning.
"It was quite aggressively bid. We've got more long bonds coming on Tuesday, so it will be interesting to see how the market handles this supply," one trader said.
The Australian Treasury is tendering A$200 million in the 10-year benchmark November 2006 and A$400 million in the September 2009 bonds on Tuesday.

Like the QTC issue, the market will be looking for a strong bid to resume the rally which took long-dated yields to 33 month lows and close to 7.0 percent on Friday. Traders said the long end is suffering a stock shortage after recent offshore demand.

Short-dated semis were also in demand last week which was partly in response to swap related activity linked to a further dual currency samurai bond issuance and saw spreads to local Treasury bonds narrow.
Two Canadian issuers, Ontario Hydro and the Province of Alberta, both launched debt in this structure totalling 80 billion yen.
Elsewhere, news that Western Australian Liberal/National coalition Premier Richard Court called a snap election for December 14 had no impact.
"Premier Court could have waited until as late as May to go to the polls, but is hoping to capitalise on recent strong performances in the opinion polls," Nomura Research Australia said in a report.
"Voters still remember the poor financial peformance of the previous Labor government that resulted in Western Australia's debt ballooning and credit rating falling from AAA to AA plus," it added.
Western Australian Treasury Corp (WATC) state bond yields and spreads moved pretty much in tandem with the rest of the market, traders added.
